node.title: First-layout domination reduces the three-petal tail to polynomially many fixed LS6 atoms
node.statement: For the rate-half M=4,t=3 FPC5 tail, fix the first admissible maximal source layout. General first-layout domination leaves at most its four planted anchors plus the complete non-planted contribution in this one layout. There are exactly four touched triples; each triple's fixed source labels determine one normalized cross-ratio, and the surviving defect parameter has fewer than n values. The exact complement-slice theorem identifies each cell with one guarded LS6 atom. Hence a uniform B(n) bound per atom gives the global bound 4nB(n)+4, with no source-layout or field-many lambda sum.
